boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Named campus spaces for studying, meeting, movement, and cultural breaks, using current university sources and access details.

cards.title: First Floor Scattered Study Areas
cards.subtitle: J.D. Williams Library
cards.notes: Set up at a table, carrel, or soft seat when conversation is acceptable; use outlets, computers, and printers as needed.
cards.short_summary: A flexible, talk-friendly library floor for solo work or informal group sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss Libraries lists this first-floor area with tables, computers, outlets, soft furniture, carrels, and a talking noise level.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces & Floor Maps | Ole Miss Libraries
cards.access_notes: Enter J.D. Williams Library from the west fountain side or descend from the east Lyceum-side stairs.

cards.entity_name: Group Work Cubicles in the Information Commons
cards.title: Information Commons Group Work Cubicles
cards.subtitle: J.D. Williams Library
cards.notes: Bring a project group to a cubicle with a projection TV, computers, printer, outlets, and large tables; talking is permitted.
cards.short_summary: A library collaboration zone equipped for shared screens and group production.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss Libraries identifies these cubicles as talking-level group study spaces with computers, a printer, and a projection TV.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces & Floor Maps | Ole Miss Libraries
cards.access_notes: Enter from the west fountain side or reach the area through Ainsworth Commons; consult library space details before reserving.

cards.entity_name: Group Work Cubicles in the Ainsworth Commons
cards.title: Ainsworth Commons Group Work Cubicles
cards.subtitle: J.D. Williams Library
cards.notes: Use the big tables, soft seating, printer, and study carrels for an active work session where conversation is permitted.
cards.short_summary: A named commons area combining group-work furniture with library service amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss Libraries lists Ainsworth Commons cubicles with group-study seating, printer access, carrels, and a talking noise level.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces & Floor Maps | Ole Miss Libraries
cards.access_notes: Enter from the west fountain side, or from the east entrance go downstairs and turn right.

cards.title: Map Room Study Area
cards.subtitle: J.D. Williams Library
cards.notes: Choose this named study area for natural light, outlets, tables, and carrels; reach it by walking through the library commons.
cards.short_summary: A bright library study stop with both table and carrel seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss Libraries describes the Map Room Study Area as a talking-level space with natural light, outlets, tables, and study carrels.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces & Floor Maps | Ole Miss Libraries
cards.access_notes: Navigate through the Information Commons and Ainsworth Commons to reach the Map Room.

cards.title: Baxter Room
cards.subtitle: J.D. Williams Library
cards.notes: Meet or work at tables with computers, a printer, outlets, soft seating, and natural light; the area is designated for talking.
cards.short_summary: A named, amenity-rich room for collaborative library work.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss Libraries lists Baxter Room as a talking-level study space with group seating, computers, printer access, outlets, and natural light.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces & Floor Maps | Ole Miss Libraries
cards.access_notes: From the west fountain entrance, go through Exhibit Hall and turn left at Starbucks.

cards.entity_name: Gertrude C. Ford Ole Miss Student Union
cards.title: Gertrude C. Ford Ole Miss Student Union
cards.subtitle: Student Union Drive
cards.notes: Use the lounge and seating areas to meet between classes, study, or attend an approved student-organization event in the building.
cards.short_summary: The university’s student-life hub with lounges, dining, organizations, and meeting spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The university calls the Student Union the center of student life and documents lounge areas, a food court, student-organization offices, and conference rooms.
cards.source_title: The Gertrude C. Ford Ole Miss Student Union | Ole Miss
cards.access_notes: The building’s published student-staff hours are Monday–Thursday 7:30 a.m.–10 p.m., Friday 7:30 a.m.–9 p.m., and weekends 10 a.m.–9 p.m.; event spaces may require reservation.

cards.title: University of Mississippi Museum
cards.subtitle: University Avenue and 5th Street
cards.notes: Plan a no-cost museum visit during public hours, then pair it with the adjacent trail or Rowan Oak grounds for a campus cultural break.
cards.short_summary: A public campus museum with free admission and regularly posted visitor information.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Mississippi Museum states that it is open to the public and that museum admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Public hours listed are Tuesday–Friday 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Saturday 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; closed Sunday, Monday, and most university holidays.

cards.title: Bailey Woods Trail
cards.subtitle: Between the University Museum and Rowan Oak
cards.notes: Walk the marked outdoor connection between the Museum and Rowan Oak; stay on the trail and use daylight for a low-key campus reset.
cards.short_summary: A free, daily outdoor route linking two university cultural destinations.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Museum states that Bailey Woods Trail is open from dawn to dusk daily and has free admission.
cards.access_notes: Open from dawn to dusk daily; a bike rack, restrooms, and water fountain are available at the Museum side entrance.

cards.title: South Campus Rail Trail
cards.subtitle: South of Highway 6, west of Chucky Mullins Drive
cards.notes: Walk, jog, or bike the marked gravel rail-bed trail, using the half-mile markers to choose an out-and-back distance that fits your time.
cards.short_summary: A five-mile round-trip campus trail with marked mileage and connected single-track routes.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss Outdoors describes the South Campus Rail Trail as a marked gravel rail bed that is five miles round trip with half-mile markers.
cards.access_notes: Located south of Highway 6 and west of Chucky Mullins Drive; university policy permits walking, jogging, and bicycling on marked trails.

cards.title: South Campus Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: 980 Whirlpool Drive
cards.notes: Use the fitness zones, courts, track, studios, or climbing wall through the appropriate campus recreation access; check current facility hours first.
cards.short_summary: A large recreation center with indoor and outdoor training, courts, track, studios, and climbing.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss Campus Recreation lists the South Campus Recreation Center’s fitness spaces, studios, courts, walking/jogging track, and indoor climbing wall.
cards.source_title: Facility Operations | Ole Miss Campus Recreation
cards.access_notes: Campus Recreation says access is controlled through turnstiles and UM students or members must present an ID; hours are subject to change.
